note.p: Mišaʾel ben ʿUzziʾel was a Qaraite scholar active in Jerusalem in the early 11th century. Little reliable information on his life is preserved. He is best known as the author of the Kitāb al-ḫilaf (Book of Differences, hebr.: Sefer ha-ḥilūfīm), a systematic account of the differences between the Masoretic traditions of Ben Ašer and Ben Naftali. Mišaʾel ben ʿUzziʾel also corrected the Torah codex, known as Cairo 3 (alternatively C3/Q3/Gottheil 18), as he informs us in its colophon, also noting that he undertook this work at the request of Maṣliaḥ b. Sahl. He corrected the codex original vocalisation and accentuation systematically towards the tradition of Ben Ašer. His annotations within the manuscript are marked with אמ (amar Mišaʾel, i.e. Mišaʾel says). Because of similar annotations and other parallels within NLR Yevr. II B 20+ has Vincent Beiler recently suggested that this manuscript was corrected by Mišaʾel ben ʿUzziʾel as well (Beiler 2023). The corrected codices together with the treatise offer a rare opportunity to examine both a scholar’s theoretical work and his own application of that knowledge in practice.
The curious case of a 12th century Geniza letter written by a Mišaʾel b. ʿUzziʾel, might be explained as being the work of a descendant bearing the same name.

note.p:
While Moritz Steinschneider (1816–1907) is primarily known for having laid
the modern foundations of Jewish bibliography, he also devoted himself to a
systematic survey of Jewish literature. In Steinschneider’s work the
investigation of Jewish writings in Arabic takes a central place. In 1845,
he proposed to the Verein für Kultur und Wissenschaft der Juden his magnum
opus , a “Jüdisch-Arabische Bibliothek” (Steinschneider, Die arabische
Literatur , xlvii). It was well received, and he obtained modest funding for
it. It seems that the first part, the Bibliotheca Judaeo-Arabica , which
consisted of a chronological survey of Judeo-Arabic literature, had already
been completed in 1845. It contained a short biographical sketch of each
author known to Steinschneider, arranged chronologically, and an account of
their works, including details of available manuscripts and translations,
mainly taken from unpublished sources. However, it only reached publication
some sixty years later with the appearance of his seminal series of articles
“An Introduction to the Arabic Literature of the Jews,” which appeared in
1897–1901 in the Jewish Quarterly Review , and also his Arabische Literatur
der Juden (1902), which Steinschneider rightly calls in its foreword his
“Lebensarbeit” (p. viii). The former, in which he describes his arduous
search for manuscripts throughout Europe, serves as a voluminous
introduction to the latter. The Arabische Literatur der Juden is divided
into seven sections: (1) Jewish authors in Ancient Arabia; (2) Jewish
authors in the East until the end of the Geonic period (1040); (3) Jewish
authors in the Muslim West; (4) Jewish in the East, 1041–1500; (5) later
Jewish authors (1500–1894); (6) Jewish authors of uncertain date; and (7)
anonymous Jewish authors according to subject.

Paul Fenton, “Moritz Steinschneider’s Contribution to Judaeo-Arabic
Studies,” in Studies on Steinschneider: Moritz Steinschneider and the
Emergence of the Science of Judaism in Nineteenth-Century Germany , edited
by Reimund Leicht and Gad Freudenthal (Leiden: Brill, 2012), pp. 363–383.

quote.p:
Mischael1) b. Ussiel, der in einem arab. Briefe an Chananel [b. Samuel §
166] um ein Darlehn bittet und als Unterpfand einige Bücher, darunter die
Makamen des Hariri und das medicinische al-Kafi [von Einzarbi, gest. 1153]
geben wollte (das Bittschreiben edirt von Jos. Horovitz, ZfHB. IV, 155, vgl.
S. 186 n. 4), verf. eine arab. Abhandl. über die Differenzen zwischen abu
Sa'id Ahron b. Moses b. Ascher und Moses b. David b. Naftali; aus einigen
defecten mss. in Pet. teilen Hk. (Chad. II, 10, Beil. zur Ztschr. ha-Mizpa,
mir unzugänglich) und Pozn. (ZfHB. IV, 186) Einiges mit; Letzterer vermutet
die Identität mit einem כתאב אלכ̇לף בין בן אשר in einer alten Bücherliste,
Jew. Qu. XIII, 52.
1) Dieser biblische Namen wurde selten; 1418 in תקנות קדמניות S. 10, 1585 s. Jew. Qu. XIV, 167 n. 48, ms. Halb. 93.
